entries.title: You choose which claims Debate checks
entries.body: In Debate, Claims lists the arguable claims an article makes, taken from the article itself, and you tick the ones worth checking, or type your own, for the AI to search the web on; Dig further searches a checked claim again. Debate's Search the web button no longer picks claims for you and looks only for responses to the piece, though claims an earlier search chose stay visible. Only an article's owner can run checks; visitors to a shared article see the list, and article downloads include your checks.

entries.title: The public library is sorted into topics
entries.body: The public library of shared articles shows topic buttons above the list, like your own library's, named by the AI from each article's title and summary; press one to see only those articles. They appear only when at least eight articles are listed, and are hidden while a topic would still name an article its owner has stopped sharing.

entries.title: Referee's Hidden text check keeps its answer
entries.body: In Referee's Hidden text view, the AI's opinions are saved with the article, so they are still there when you reload, along with the day you asked. If you leave the page while the check is running, it finishes and is kept rather than lost, and your article download includes it.

entries.title: Help pages open with a short summary
entries.body: Each mode's Help page starts with a brief explanation and, where there is one, its main picture, with the fuller account below under How it works. The Ask about Spideryarn box on the Help page also has a microphone, so you can speak your question instead of typing it.

entries.title: The AI uses newer default versions
entries.body: New AI work across the reading modes, article chat, Help answers and turning PDFs you add into text uses newer versions of the AI services by default. The privacy page lists which ones are used.

entries.title: Dictated words stay in the right box
entries.body: If you dictated into a comment, a note, a Quiz answer or a Feedback reply and moved on to another before the words arrived, they could land in the wrong box. They are held back instead, and a message asks you to go back and press Try again, which reuses what was already written out.

entries.title: The More button stays reachable on a phone
entries.body: On a phone, when Diagram was showing in the mode bar at the bottom of the screen, the More button sat past the right edge and could only be reached by scrolling the bar. When it would not fit, it moves to the front of the bar instead.
